**Calculation**

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 |
|---|---|---|
| R&D expense | $29,915M [DOC-1] | $31,370M [DOC-1] |
| Revenue | $383,285M [DOC-1] | $391,035M [DOC-1] |
| R&D as % of revenue | 7.80% | 8.02% |

- FY2023: $29,915M ÷ $383,285M = 7.805% [DOC-1]
- FY2024: $31,370M ÷ $391,035M = 8.022% [DOC-1]
- Change: 8.022% − 7.805% = **+0.22 percentage points (increase)**

**Comparability note:** Both figures are drawn from the same filing (Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K, accession 0000320193-24-000123), so the accounting basis, entity, and expense classification are consistent [DOC-1]. One caveat not resolvable from the excerpt: Apple's fiscal years are 52/53-week periods, so if the two years differ in length, the revenue and expense bases would not be strictly week-for-week comparable — though the ratio (a percentage of revenue) is far less sensitive to that than the absolute dollar growth figures would be.

R&D grew ~4.9% while revenue grew ~2.0%, which is why the ratio rose [DOC-1].

ANSWER: Increased by approximately 0.22 percentage points (from ~7.80% in FY2023 to ~8.02% in FY2024)
